strings.name: Ferenc Krausz
strings.summary: Born in Mór, Hungary, Krausz studied electrical engineering and theoretical physics in Budapest before doctoral training in Vienna. He and his team developed ultrashort lasers and generated and measured isolated attosecond pulses in 2001, enabling studies of electron motion. He built research facilities in Germany and extended measurements to matter and biological molecules. He shared the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics and joined HKU in 2025 to continue laser and attosecond research.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced attosecond physics experiments and ultrafast optics, developing techniques to probe dynamic electronic processes in matter.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Electrical engineering degree, Budapest University of Technology (1985), alongside theoretical physics studies; doctorate, Vienna University of Technology (1991).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Isolated attosecond pulses
strings.highlights.h1.text: Generated and measured isolated attosecond pulses with his team, bringing ultrafast electronic processes into experiments.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Interdisciplinary ultrafast measurement
strings.highlights.h2.text: Developed laser and precision-measurement facilities connecting electron dynamics and molecular research.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joining HKU
strings.timeline.t1.text: Became a physics chair professor, extending laser and attosecond research to Hong Kong.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Shared the award for attosecond-pulse experimental methods with Agostini and L’Huillier.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Sharing the Wolf Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t3.text: Recognized with two fellow researchers for ultrafast lasers and attosecond science.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Munich professorship
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became an experimental physics professor in Germany, developing laser and electron-dynamics research.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Max Planck directorship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Established attosecond research in Garching, collaborating with German universities and teams.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Isolated attosecond pulses
strings.timeline.t6.text: Generated and measured ultrashort pulses with colleagues to study electron motion in real time.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Vienna doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned a doctorate in laser physics and continued ultrafast laser research.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing Budapest engineering studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned an electrical engineering degree while also studying theoretical physics at another university.
